### Page note: https://www.ppic.org/wp-content/uploads/s-518mbs.pdf
Reader state: complete; relevance: partial
**Page:** *PPIC STATEWIDE SURVEY – Most Important Issues* (PDF page 14) – https://www.ppic.org/wp-content/uploads/s-518mbs.pdf  
**Evidence:**  

| Issue (most important) | All (%) | San Francisco Bay Area (%) | Likely adults (%) | Central Valley (%) | Inland Empire (%) | Los Angeles (%) | Orange/San Diego (%) |
|------------------------|--------|----------------------------|-------------------|--------------------|-------------------|------------------|----------------------|
| Jobs, economy | 18% | 18% | 22% | 18% | 17% | **20%** | 15% |
| Immigration, illegal immigration | 15% | 17% | 15% | 15% | 17% | 11% | 19% |
| Housing costs, housing availability | 9% | 4% | 7% | 7% | 9% | **21%** | 9% |

*Additional textual support:*  
“Californians are most likely to name either jobs and the economy (18% adults) or immigration (15% adults) as the most important issue”. (page 14)

**Coverage:**  
- Regionally disaggregated top‑issue percentages for all adults.  
- Values for Los Angeles and Central Valley regions.  
- State‑wide adult percentages >9% (jobs/economy, immigration).  
- Los Angeles percentages >12% for jobs and housing.  
- Central Valley percentages (jobs 18%, immigration 15%, housing 7%).  

**Missing:**  
- No evidence on any issue that simultaneously receives >12% of Los Angeles respondents and between 10–14% of Central Valley respondents as the top issue.

None provided in the supplied content.
